Rashi on Pesachim 23b:11:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה מהיכא דנפקא ליה לרבי יהודה - לעיל, אליבא דרבי אבהו, דמייתי ליה: מאותו אתה משליך לכלב, ואי אתה משליך שאר איסורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:11:1.english: And let him derive it from where Rabbi Yehuda derives it - [As stated] above, according to Rabbi Abbahu, who cited it from: “'It' you may cast to the dog, but you may not cast other prohibited items [to the dog].”

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:12:2.hebrew: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה - אסורין בהנאה מדאורייתא, ונפקא ליה מאותו, ומיבעי ליה קרא אחרינא לשאר איסורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:12:2.english: Non-sacrificial animals that were slaughtered in the courtyard - [They] are forbidden from benefit by Torah law, and he derives this from “it” [“you shall cast it to the dog”], and [therefore] he requires another verse for the other prohibitions.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:12:3.hebrew: כל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה - לאו בחטאות הפנימיות שהובא דמן כמצוותן לפנים כתיב, דהא בהדיא כתיב בהן — בפר כהן משיח והעלם דבר — שריפתן מחוץ למחנה; אלא ללמד על חטאת החיצונה, דאם הכניס דמה לפנים — פסולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:12:3.english: “Any sin-offering of which [any] of its blood is brought” - [This] is not written regarding the inner sin-offerings, whose blood was brought inside in accordance with their commandment, for behold, it is explicitly written regarding them — in [the passages of] the bull of the anointed priest and [the bull of] an overlooked matter — [that] their burning is outside the camp. Rather, [it is] to teach regarding an outer sin-offering, that if one brought its blood inside, it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:13:1.hebrew: אם אינו ענין לגופו דהא כתיב והנה שורף - בשעיר נחשון, ב"ויהי ביום השמיני", וקאמר להו משה: למה שרפתם אותו? "הן לא הובא את דמה אל הקדש פנימה" — מכלל דאם הובא, שפיר עבוד דשרפוה, אלמא בת שריפה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:13:1.english: If it does not apply to the subject matter itself, as it is written: “and, behold, it was burnt” - Regarding the goat of Nachshon, in [the passage of] “And it came to pass on the eighth day” (Leviticus 9–10). And Moshe said to them: Why did you burn it? “Behold, its blood was not brought into the sanctuary within” (Leviticus 10:18) — by implication, had it been brought [in], they would have acted properly by burning it; evidently, it is subject to burning.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:13:2.hebrew: לכל איסורין - שנאמר בהן לאו באכילתן כזה, ועל כרחיך לא מייתי אלא חמץ בפסח ושור הנסקל, דבשאר איסורים כתיב פרטא להיתירא:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:13:2.english: To all prohibitions - In which a negative commandment is stated regarding their eating, like this [case]. And perforce, it includes only leavened bread on Passover and an ox that is stoned, for regarding other prohibitions, a specific verse is written permitting [benefit].

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:2:1.hebrew: חלבה וגידה לא הותרו - דחלב אינו בכלל בשר, הלכך לא הוה במשמע תתננה ואכלה, וגבי נוגע בנבלתה נמי לאו חלב במשמע. הלכך, יעשה לכל מלאכה לא הוצרך לטהרו, אלא להתירו מכלל הנאות לא תאכל חלב:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:2:1.english: Its fat and its sinew were not permitted - For fat is not included in [the category of] meat; therefore, it was not implied by: "You may give it and he may eat it" [or sell it], and regarding: "[He who] touches its carcass," fat is also not implied. Therefore, "It may be used for any service" was not needed to declare it pure, but rather to permit it from the general [prohibition of] benefit [implied by]: "You shall not eat fat."

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:2:2.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא סבר - חלב בכלל נבילה, בין להיתר הנאה בין לטמא. הלכך, כי איצטריך קרא — לטהרו איצטריך:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:2:2.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds - Fat is included in [the category of] a carcass, both regarding permission to derive benefit and regarding defilement. Therefore, when the verse was necessary, it was necessary to declare it pure.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:4:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון - דאמר לעיל: גיד אסור בהנאה, משום דסבירא ליה: אין בגידין בנותן טעם, ולא הותר בכלל נבילה — מאי טעמא לא מייתי ליה כרבי יוסי להתיר הנאה מקל וחומר מחלב:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:4:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon - Who said above that deriving benefit from the [sciatic] nerve is prohibited, because he holds that sinews do not impart flavor and [therefore it] was not permitted within the general category of carrion — what is the reason that he does not derive it like Rabbi Yose, to permit [deriving] benefit through an a fortiori inference from fat?

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:4:2.english: From its general [prohibition] - [It was permitted] even for eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:5:1.hebrew: ואידך - רבי יוסי אמר לך: אנא בחלב בהמה קא מייתינא קרא להתיר בהנאה, דקרא בחלב שור וכשב קאי וקא שרי ליה בהנאה, ובבהמה לא הותר מכללו באכילה. הלכך, אתי גיד הנשה מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:5:1.english: And the other - Rabbi Yosei [could] say to you: I am citing the verse regarding the fat of a domesticated animal to permit [it] for benefit, for the verse refers to the fat of an ox and a sheep and permits it for benefit, and with regard to a domesticated animal, [its fat] was not released from its general [prohibition] against eating. Therefore, [the law of] the sciatic nerve can be derived from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:1.hebrew: מכדי אותבינהו כל הנך קראי - דכל איסורין שנאמ' בהן "לא תאכל", ומותרין בהנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:1.english: Now, since we raised objections [from] all those verses - That with regard to all forbidden items concerning which "You shall not eat" is stated, they are [nevertheless] permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:2.hebrew: ושנינהו - רבי אבהו, ואשכח בהו פרטא להיתר. לא מצינו באחד מכולם שהחמיר בו ר' אבהו ויאמר שאסור בהנאה ולחזקיה לישתרו, אלא דבר האסור אסור לדברי שניהן, והמותר מותר לדברי שניהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:2.english: And answered them - Rabbi Abbahu [answered them], and found in them a specific exclusion permitting [benefit]. We have not found in a single one of all of them that Rabbi Abbahu was stringent with regard to it, saying that it is forbidden to derive benefit, while according to Ḥizkiya it would be permitted; rather, whatever is forbidden is forbidden according to both of them, and whatever is permitted is permitted according to both of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:3.hebrew: במאי פליגי - דאין לך איסורי הנאה בדבר שנאמר בו לאו באכילתו שלא נאמר בו פרט להתיר, אלא הנך שני דברים דכתיב בהן לא יאכל — כגון שור הנסקל וחמץ בפסח — ובין למר ובין למר אסורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:3.english: With regard to what do they disagree - For you have no items forbidden from [deriving] benefit among anything regarding which a negative prohibition was stated concerning its eating where a specific [clause] was not stated to permit [it], except for those two things in which “it shall not be eaten” is written — such as an ox that is stoned and leavened bread on Passover — and according to both this Master and that Master, they are forbidden [from benefit].

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:4.hebrew: ואליבא דרבנן - דפליגי עליה דרבי יוסי, דאמר לעיל: חמץ בפסח מותר בהנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:4.english: And in accordance with the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi Yosei, who said above: Chametz on Passover is permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:5.hebrew: מנבילה - מדאיצטריך קרא למישרי נבילה, ואי הוה כתיב לא תאכל נמי הוה מיתסרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:6:5.english: From [an animal] carcass - From [the fact] that Scripture needed to permit [benefit from] a carcass; and [thus,] even if "You shall not eat" had been written, they would also have been forbidden [from deriving benefit].

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:7:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו חולין שנשחטו בעזרה - ואליבא דר' יהודה, דאמר: מנבילה לא מצי למיגמר, דלדברים ככתבן אתא. דחזקיה סבר: הני תרי, מדשני בדיבוריה — איתסר; ו"לכלב תשליכון אותו" לא הוצרך למעט את אלו ולאוסרן בהנאה, וכי אתא — למעוטי חולין שנשחטו בעזרה אתא, וכדפרישית לעיל. ורבי אבהו סבר: אין חילוק בין "לא יאכל" בין "לא יאכל", ואצטריך "אותו" למעוטי הני. והכי משמע: טריפה, אף על גב שכתבתי לך לאו באכילתה — אני מתיר לך הנאתה; אבל לא חמץ ושור הנסקל, שלא פרטתי לך בהן היתר:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:7:1.english: The practical difference between them is non-sacrificial [animals] slaughtered in the [Temple] Courtyard - And [this is] in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that] one cannot learn from [an animal] carcass, for it came for its words as they are written. For Ḥizkiya holds: These two [items], since [the Torah] changed its phrasing, were prohibited [from benefit]; and “you shall cast it to the dog” was not needed to exclude these and prohibit them from benefit; and when it came [to make an exclusion], it came to exclude non-sacrificial [animals] slaughtered in the [Temple] Courtyard, and as I explained above. And Rabbi Abbahu holds: There is no distinction between “it shall not be eaten” and “it shall not be eaten” [whether phrased passively or actively], and “it” was needed to exclude these. And this is what it means: [Regarding] a torn [animal (tereifah)], even though I wrote for you a negative commandment regarding its eating, I permit its benefit to you; but not leavened bread and an ox that is stoned, in which I did not specify permission for you.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:8:1.hebrew: חולין בעזרה לאו דאורייתא - וכי אמר רבי אבהו ״לא יאכל איסור הנאה משמע״ — אליבא דרבי מאיר אמרה, דלית ליה ״לדברים ככתבן״; ומדאיצטריך למישרי נבילה — מכלל דשאר איסורין, כגון חמץ ושור הנסקל, אסירי; ולאו משום שינוי הלשון, שאין חילוק בין ״לא יאכל״ ל״לא יאכל״ לרבי אבהו, אלא מדאיצטריך למישרי נבילה. ו״אותו״ לר"מ — למעוטי חולין בעזרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:8:1.english: Non-sacrificial animals in the [Temple] courtyard are not by Torah law - And when Rabbi Abbahu stated: '“It shall not be eaten” implies a prohibition of benefit,' he stated it according to Rabbi Meir, who does not hold [that the verse comes merely] 'according to its literal wording'; and since it was necessary [for the Torah] to permit [an animal] carcass, it follows that other prohibited items, such as leaven and an ox that is stoned, are forbidden [in benefit] — and [this is] not on account of a change in wording, for there is no distinction between [passive] 'it shall not be eaten' and [active] 'he shall not eat' according to Rabbi Abbahu, but rather because it was necessary to permit [an animal] carcass. And 'it' [“you shall cast it to the dogs”], according to Rabbi Meir, [comes] to exclude non-sacrificial animals [slaughtered] in the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 23b:9:1.hebrew: ה"ג - ומאי נינהו — חמץ בפסח ושור הנסקל:
Rashi on Pesachim 23b:9:1.english: This is the reading - And what are they? Leavened bread on Passover and an ox that is stoned.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:13:1.hebrew: דכתיב והנה שורף - פרש"י בשעיר נחשון, ובת"כ דריש בהדיא אשעיר דראש חודש, מדכתיב: "ואותה נתן לכם" וגו' — והיינו של ר"ח, דמכפר עון על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:13:1.english: “As it is written: And, behold, it was burnt” - Rashi explains [that this refers to] the goat of Nachshon. But in Torat Kohanim, it explicitly expounds [it] regarding the goat of Rosh Chodesh, as it is written: “And He has given it to you” etc. (Leviticus 10:17) — and that is [the offering] of Rosh Chodesh, which atones for the sin regarding defilement of the Sanctuary and its sacred items.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:13:2.hebrew: דהא כתיב והנה שורף - פרש"י: ואמר להו משה: "הן לא הובא את דמה אל הקדש פנימה" — מכלל דאם הובא, שפיר עבוד דשרפוה. הקשה הרב רבינו שלמה מטרויש: הא על כרחיך לאו שפיר עבוד דשרפוה, דהא שרפוה בלא עיבור צורה! ואמר בפרק כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים פב:): "כל שפסולו בגופו ישרף מיד, בדם ובבעלים תעובר צורתו ויצא לשריפה". וקרא ה"ק: "מדוע לא אכלתם את החטאת, הן לא הובא את דמה" — הא אם הובא, שפיר עבוד דלא אכלוה. ואומר ר"י דה"פ: "אם אינו ענין לגופה" — דהא קיי"ל בפרק כיצד צולין (גם זה שם): "כל שפסולו בקדש בשריפה", וחטאת דאהרן משום מעשה שהיה; "תנהו לכל איסורים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:13:2.english: "For it is written: 'And, behold, it was burnt'" - Rashi explained: And Moshe said to them: "Behold, its blood was not brought into the Sanctuary within" (Leviticus 10:18) — implying that if it had been brought, they acted properly in that they burnt it. The Rabbi, Rabbeinu Shlomo of Troyes, raised a difficulty: Behold, of necessity they did not act properly in that they burnt it, for they burnt it without [waiting for] its form to deteriorate! And it says in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 82b): "Anything whose disqualification is in its body shall be burnt immediately; [if the disqualification is] in the blood or in the owners, its form must deteriorate and [only then] go out to the burning." And this is what the verse is saying: "Why did you not eat the sin-offering... Behold, its blood was not brought" — that is, if it had been brought, they acted properly that they did not eat it. And the Ri says that this is its explanation: "If it is not needed for its own matter" — for we maintain in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (this too is there): "Anything whose disqualification [occurred] in the sacred area is subject to burning," and [the incident of] Aaron's sin-offering was [stated merely] because of an event that occurred; [therefore,] "apply it to all prohibitions [in the Torah]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:3:1.hebrew: ומה חלב שענוש כרת מותר בהנאה - וא"ת: לימא, שור הנסקל ושאר איסורי הנאה יוכיחו, שאינן בכרת ואפ"ה אסורין בהנאה? וי"ל, דה"פ: ומה חלב שענוש כרת ואסור באכילה, ומותר בהנאה כמו נבילה עצמה — גיד שאין ענוש כרת, לכ"ש שיהא בכלל היתר נבילה! והשתא לא שייך למימר "תוכיח". ולא מצי למיעבד נמי ק"ו מדם, דדם אינו בכלל נבילה, ואפילו טומאה אין בו מטעם נבילה, כדפרישי' לעיל (פסחים דף כב.). אבל חלב הוה שפיר בכלל נבילה, דלטומאה לא הוה צריך קרא, דאדרבה, לטהרו מידי נבילה מצריך קרא. והא דקאמר: "היא הותרה וחלבה לא הותרה", לאו משום דלא הוי בכלל נבילה, אלא משום דלא הותרה בנבילה אלא מה שהותר בטהורה באכילה. והשתא א"ש הא דקאמר: "ואידך, אנן בבהמה קיימינן" — דלא ילפינן אלא שיהא בכלל היתר נבילה, אבל בעלמא מודה דפריך שפיר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:3:1.english: "And if fat, for which one is punished with karet, is permitted for benefit" - And if you say: Let [the case of] the ox that is stoned and other items forbidden for benefit prove [otherwise], as they do not carry [the punishment of] karet and nevertheless are forbidden for benefit? And one can say that this is the explanation: If fat, which is punishable with karet and forbidden for eating, is permitted for benefit just like a carcass itself — [the sciatic] nerve, which is not punishable with karet, all the more so should it be included in the dispensation of a carcass! And now, it is not applicable to say "let [them] prove [otherwise]." And one could also not make an a fortiori inference from blood, for blood is not in the category of a carcass, and it does not even contract ritual impurity on account of [being a] carcass, as we explained above (Pesachim 22a). However, fat is indeed properly in the category of a carcass, for regarding ritual impurity it would not have required a verse [to render it impure], for on the contrary, it required a verse to purify it from [the impurity of] a carcass. And that which [the Gemara] said: "It was permitted, but its fat was not permitted," is not because it is not in the category of a carcass, but rather because nothing was permitted in a carcass except that which was permitted for eating in a kosher [animal]. And now, that which [the Gemara] said: "And the other? We are dealing with [a domesticated] animal" is well understood: For we are only learning that it should be included in the dispensation of a carcass, but in general he concedes that [the Gemara] refutes well.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:5:1.hebrew: בבהמה מיהא לא אישתרי - אין להקשות: דגיד חיה מיהא ליתסר — דכיון דשל בהמה לא מיתסר בהנאה, אם כן "לא יאכל" דכתיב גבי גיד הנשה — באכילה דוקא קאמר; ומהיכא תיתי לן לאסור של חיה בהנאה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:5:1.english: "With regard to a domesticated animal, in any case, it is not permitted" - One should not object: Let the [sciatic] nerve of a wild animal, in any case, be forbidden [from benefit]! For since that of a domesticated animal is not forbidden from benefit, if so, "it shall not be eaten" that is written regarding the sciatic nerve speaks specifically of eating; and from where would it be derived for us to prohibit that of a wild animal from benefit?

Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:7:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - תימה לרשב"א: לימא דאיכא בינייהו חמץ נוקשה וחמץ דגן גמור ע"י תערובות, דמרבינן בריש אלו עוברין (לקמן פסחים מג.) מ"כל מחמצת לא תאכלו" — דלחזקיה מותר בהנאה, ולרבי אבהו: כל מקום שנאמר "לא תאכלו" משמע איסור הנאה. וכי תימא: כיון דמרבינן ליה לאכילה, ה"ה להנאה — אם כן, כרת נמי ליחייב:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23b:7:1.english: What is [the practical difference] between them - The Rashba finds this difficult: Let [the Gemara] say that [the difference] between them is chametz nuksheh [inferior leaven] and full-fledged grain chametz via a mixture, which we include at the beginning of [the chapter] Elu Ovrin (below, Pesachim 43a) from "You shall eat nothing leavened" [kol machmetzet lo tokhelu] — for according to Ḥizkiya [they are] permitted for benefit, whereas according to Rabbi Abbahu, wherever it is stated "You shall not eat" [lo tokhelu], it implies a prohibition of benefit. And if you were to say: Since we include it for eating, the same applies to benefit — if so, let one also be liable to karet!
